key_insight: Matching data across the two zeroth-order finite-difference evaluations cancels oracle-noise amplification, whereas mismatched on-policy evaluations amplify it by 1/μ².
engineering_relevance: ZO-BOLT offers a path to more reliable, memory-efficient LLM post-training by pairing matched-data optimization with an RLVR-aligned objective.
method: Analyze gradient-estimator variance under matched versus mismatched data.
Derive convergence guarantees with explicit constants separating the two regimes.
Build ZO-BOLT on Boltzmann Targeted SFT’s matched-data advantage.
evidence_signal: Perturbation-scale sweeps and matched-versus-mismatched comparisons support the predicted effect; tests across three models and two mathematical reasoning benchmarks show consistent gains over pretrained baselines with near-inference memory use.
watch_item: Matched-data cancellation removes the identified amplification mechanism, not all estimation noise; broader task generalization is not established by the reported math benchmarks.
paper_title: The Cost of Mismatch: Noise Amplification in Zeroth-Order Reinforcement Learning
